cd-rock-falls-days-grove-1906.st: The picnics went on for decades. The 6th annual Rock Falls Co-op Creamery picnic was in Day's grove in August 1908, with 400 to 500 people (Dunn County News, 20 Aug 1908, p. 1). In August 1923 about 1,000 people gathered in "Day's pine grove in Rock Falls" (Dunn County News, 30 Aug 1923, p. 1). The Dunn County News mentions the grove 23 times from 1908 to 1930, with picnics in 1913, 1925 and 1928-30, so it was a yearly crowd site for about 27 years. Being a pine grove "in Rock Falls", it was in or right beside the village.

d-carson-park.st: Confirmed: in January 1914 the Carson heirs deeded "Half Moon Lake island or Horseshoe Island" to the City of Eau Claire for a natural park (Eau Claire Leader, 17 Jan 1914, p. 5). So the Horseshoe Island dance pavilion, the Fourth of July grounds and the union balls of about 1903-1913 were on today's Carson Park, before it became a city park.
